solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Young girl returned with neat recast jewellery

indicators.note: returned means the word for the young girl is sent back the other way

parts.note: a maid is an old word for a young girl

indicators.note: recast means the letters of neat are cast again in a new shape

explanation.surface: A young woman comes home wearing a freshly remodelled piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns MAID into DIAM; 'recast' turns NEAT into ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamante is sparkling costume jewellery or trimming made of paste or glass stones.

clue.text: Unhappy, put back start of horse race

indicators.note: put back means the word for unhappy is written in reverse order

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: start of picks out the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A gloomy punter whose horse race start was postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a short sprint, a quick race over a brief distance.

clue.text: Cash in one's chips in gold — farewell!

indicators.note: in says the word for dying sits inside the symbol for gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to cash in one's chips is an idiom meaning to die

explanation.surface: A gambler bids goodbye after cashing in chips for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French-derived word of parting, used in English as a goodbye.

clue.text: Eccentric lent Patricia something tiny

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters that follow are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: An odd person lent a tiny something to a woman named Patricia.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiparticle is a subatomic particle, about as small as physical things get.

clue.text: Christmas fare in the country

definitions.meaning: the bird roasted for the traditional festive dinner
the nation spanning Anatolia and part of the Balkans, capital Ankara

explanation.definitionFit: The festive roast bird and the nation straddling Europe and Asia share one name.

clue.text: Wading bird, one initially breeding in swamps

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A wading bird is seen breeding in the swamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers all three of breeding, in and swamps, giving BIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill.

clue.text: Like a city pub, lit badly outside university

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for university
badly means the letters of pub and lit are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A poorly lit pub on the edge of a university in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges PUB and LIT into BUILTP, which goes 'outside' U.
explanation.definitionFit: Built-up land is densely covered with buildings, as an urban area is.

clue.text: Normal place taxis stop on a road

parts.note: a taxi stand or taxi rank is where cabs wait

explanation.surface: It is normal for the taxi rank to be on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard as an adjective means usual or ordinary, the accepted norm.

clue.text: Mounted contest in very expensive rental contract involving church

parts.note: steep is informal for overpriced

indicators.note: involving means the contract wraps around the abbreviation for church

parts.note: a lease is a contract for renting property

explanation.surface: A church's pricey lease leads to a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse race over fences, a contest for riders on horseback.

clue.text: Son isn't a very good person

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A parent laments that their son is not a very good person.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is someone exceptionally virtuous, a paragon of goodness.

clue.text: Sent back topless container for Greek wine

indicators.note: sent back means the shortened container word is read in reverse
topless means the first letter of the container word is removed

parts.note: a canister is a container, typically for tea or coffee

explanation.surface: A wine was returned because its container had no lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts CANISTER to ANISTER; 'Sent back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a white or rosé wine from Greece flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Flexible chaps, with Edward being given extra

parts.note: supple means bendy or flexible
chaps means men
Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Bendy blokes and a man named Edward get a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: To be supplemented is to have something added as a top-up.

clue.text: Supports crown as a last resort?

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
the crown of something is its top

explanation.surface: Using a crown to prop something up only in desperation.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstop is a final safeguard, the fallback used when all else fails.

clue.text: Commercial has to avoid including director's head

indicators.note: including means the word for avoid takes in the director's first letter

parts.note: to avert danger is to avoid it

indicators.note: head picks out the opening letter of director's

explanation.surface: A commercial must sidestep featuring the director at its forefront.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is an advertisement, a commercial on screen or in print.

clue.text: Criminal is bad in vain

indicators.note: in says the word for bad sits within vain

parts.note: ill can mean bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer whose bad deeds were all for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wrongdoer, a criminal in the police sense.

clue.text: Concerning east European travelling west — runaway bride

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means reading right to left

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a Pole comes from Poland in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A bride from eastern Europe heads west to flee her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: An eloper is someone who runs off secretly to marry, so a fleeing bride fits.

clue.text: Equine swallowing second piece of hay is croaking

indicators.note: swallowing means the animal takes in the letter from hay

parts.note: an equine is a horse

indicators.note: second piece of picks the middle letter of hay

explanation.surface: A horse eating hay makes a croaking noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarse voice is rough and croaky, as with a sore throat.

clue.text: I looked space all around with optical device

indicators.note: all around means the letters are spun about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone peers into the space all around them with an optical device.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaleidoscope is a tube of mirrors and coloured pieces making shifting patterns, an optical toy.

clue.text: Songbird — it goes after seed

indicators.note: goes after places it behind the word for seed

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: A songbird pursues a seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small brown songbird of open country.

clue.text: Group of animals caught, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word for caught is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so caught means heard

explanation.surface: A group of animals were reportedly captured.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of cattle, deer or similar grazing animals.

clue.text: Something for transporting creeping plant

definitions.meaning: an unpowered wheeled vehicle towed behind a car or lorry to carry loads
a plant that trails along the ground or hangs down

explanation.surface: A vehicle carrying a creeping plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the towed vehicle and a trailing plant go by this one word.

clue.text: More than enough to taste without needing seconds

indicators.note: without needing means the abbreviation for seconds is dropped from the word for taste

parts.note: to sample food is to taste it

explanation.surface: A diner has had plenty just tasting, with no need for second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like extra helpings but is S for seconds of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, enough or more than is required.

clue.text: Some tarpon deep in artificial lake

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few tarpon fish lie deep in a man-made lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'in', but 'in' is the link word; 'artificial lake' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond is a small body of still water, often dug or made by people.

clue.text: Mentioned again grass contains burnable plant matter

indicators.note: contains means the grass word holds the fuel word inside

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
peat is decayed plant material cut and burnt as fuel

explanation.surface: A repeated remark that grass holds combustible plant matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated means said or done once more, so mentioned a second time.
